correctness.rationale: For q>3 prime and a,b,c>=1, the exact totient product gives T(2^a3^bq^c)=2^a3^(b-1)q^(c-1)(2q+1). The final factor is odd, congruent to one mod q and exceeds one; requiring no new prime forces 2q+1=3^h with h>=3, independent of exponent triple. Conversely this identity reduces q exponent c times and raises 3 exponent by (h-1) each time. Then T(2^u3^v)=2^(u+1)3^(v-1) for v>0, and T(2^u)=2^(u-1), giving all three displayed orbit segments, height a+2b+(2h-1)c and parity SG=a+c mod2. Independent trial-division totients verified q=13,1093 on three exponent triples each. No unproved assertion of infinitely many eligible q.
residual_risks: At n=1 map is terminal; no extension T(1)=0. Other support families and q with factor leakage excluded.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior two-prime orbit family is narrower in starting support. Lemma 4.4 of Ellis et al. handles multiplying 2-power factors, but does not supply the 2q+1 ternary condition or all c q-steps by itself.

originality.rationale: Ellis–Shi–Thanatipanonda–Tu Theorem 4.2 settles a two-prime p^k q^l support under q=p^b-p+1. This three-prime 2^a3^bq^c closure requires the new factor 2q+1=3^h and a distinct three-stage orbit length. Iannucci–Larsson defines the NONTOTIENT game and examines basic families, not the exact three-prime classification. These checked results do not imply the entire three-prime claim by merely substituting parameters, although the later two-prime stage relies on familiar totient identities.
residual_risks: Possible unindexed elementary number-theory treatment; this sharp three-prime formula may be easy to rediscover, so priority is best-of-knowledge.

Its simple factors do not make it merely a one-instance evaluation; no general-support claims are made.
